title: Paralyzed at 11. Paralympic gold medalist twice over. October 24, 2026.
excerpt: From India's seat at the UN's founding before its own independence, to a defence company's third big export win in six months, to an ambulance sent home from Riyadh in a mother's memory, October 24's five stories are about showing up before you're fully ready, and still delivering.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about arriving at something before the usual conditions were in place - a UN seat secured before full sovereignty, an honour built on training from one country applied in another, an export order landing on the back of two before it, a gift sent home from thousands of kilometres away, and a gold medal won by someone who'd been paralyzed only three years earlier.

October 24, 1945: the United Nations Charter took effect - and India had already signed it, two years before its own independence

India was a founding member of the United Nations, signing the Charter at the San Francisco Conference in June 1945 while still under British rule - a seat at the world's premier international body secured before the country had full control of its own government.

She trained in Kerala and Bangalore before building a career in Australian child psychiatry. In 2026, the King honoured her for it

Professor Valsamma Eapen was named an Officer of the Order of Australia in the 2026 King's Birthday Honours, recognizing her neurodevelopmental research at UNSW Sydney, built on training that began at India's National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences.

An NRI in Saudi Arabia just gave his hometown a free ambulance, in his mother's memory

Raja Sood, an NRI based in Riyadh, donated an ambulance to the Palampur Sani Sewa Sadan in Himachal Pradesh in memory of his late mother - a gift sent home from thousands of kilometres away. (Note: based on a single news report; independent confirmation not found as of publication.)

An Indian defence company just won a Rs 1,076 crore order from overseas clients

Solar Industries India secured a Rs 1,076 crore defence export order in May 2026 - its third major export win in roughly six months, following a Rs 1,400 crore order in November 2025 and an Rs 830 crore order in January 2026.

Paralyzed at 11. Paralympic gold medalist twice over

A 2012 car accident left Avani Lekhara paralyzed below the waist. She took up shooting in 2015 and became the first Indian woman to win Paralympic gold at Tokyo 2020, then defended her title at Paris 2024 with a new record score - only the second Indian athlete ever to win two Paralympic golds.

Five stories, one pattern: a UN seat claimed before full independence, an honour built on training from one country and applied in another, a gift sent home across a continent, an export record building on the two before it, and a gold medal won by someone who'd lost the use of her legs only three years before she won it.
